name: Brahmani

source.name: Confluence of the Sankh and South Koel rivers at Vedavyas, near Rourkela

sink.name: Brahmani-Baitarani joint delta, near Dhamra
sink.location: Bhadrak district, Odisha, Bay of Bengal

did_you_know: The Brahmani is formed not by a single spring but by the confluence of the Sankh and South Koel rivers near the industrial town of Rourkela.
It is one of the few Indian rivers that cuts across the Eastern Ghats, carving a small gorge at Rengali where a dam has been built.
Together with the Baitarani, the Brahmani forms a large joint delta at Dhamra that includes the Bhitarkanika mangroves, a key nesting site for estuarine crocodiles.
